evals.expected_output: Skill reads references/usage.md and presents the walkthrough (what it does, the three modes, examples, edge cases). Does NOT run an audit.

assertions.rationale: Help mode must NOT emit Mode A/B/C section headers — that would mean an audit ran.

evals.expected_output: Same behavior as 'help'. Alias coverage: --help / -h / ? all route to help mode and stop.
Mode A activates. Output has all 6 sections (What's working, Sharpen, Cut, Add, Cite or soften, Bottom-line check) plus the single highest-leverage change at the end.

assertions.rationale: The closing recommendation is load-bearing — without it the audit reads as a list, not a verdict.

evals.expected_output: Mode A activates on the primary target (a /focus-group culmination report). Sharpening pass focuses on what to fix before the user sends the report on.
Skill says the file doesn't exist plainly. Does not attempt the audit. Does not invent content.

assertions.rationale: No audit may run on a missing file — emitting section headers would mean fabricated content.

evals.expected_output: Mode B activates. Reads focus-group SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/ + config.json + README/index.html mentions. Output has 7 sections including the new Description triggering section.
Skill lists the 6 valid skill names and asks which the user meant. Does not attempt to audit a nonexistent skill.

assertions.rationale: Must enumerate valid skill names rather than fail opaquely.
No audit content may be generated for a nonexistent skill.

evals.expected_output: Mode C activates. On a workspace with no .scratch/focus-group/ history and no .org-profile.json, the skill says so plainly and suggests running /focus-group once before re-invoking. Does not invent usage patterns.

assertions.pattern: ## What I learned about your usage
assertions.rationale: No usage-pattern bullets may be invented when the workspace has no state.

evals.prompt: I'm worried this Q3 forecast is wrong. Can you help me think about it?
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT auto-activate. The user did not invoke /how-can-this-be-improved, used no trigger phrases (no 'how can this be improved', no 'audit this report', no 'sharpen this'). This is adjacent review-talk, not an invocation.

assertions.pattern: (## What's working|## Sharpen|## Strengths|## Top 3 changes)
assertions.rationale: Skill must not auto-trigger on adjacent talk that lacks the explicit invocation.

evals.expected_output: Argument has a path-like shape (.md extension). Skill treats this as Mode A and tries the file first. If the file doesn't exist, the skill says so (does NOT silently fall back to Mode B on the bare 'focus-group' string).

assertions.rationale: The .md extension is the user's explicit signal for Mode A — the skill must not silently switch modes.
Mode B section header would indicate an unwanted silent fallback.
